notes.2: Few candidates chose Distractor A or Distractor B. Weaker candidates were more likely to choose Distractor C, the diagram which represents a single compound only.
notes.3: This question was not well answered. Many candidates appeared to confuse the number of electrons in the outer shell with the number of electron shells and chose Distractor C.
notes.5: The more able candidates had little difficulty with this question whereas none of the less able candidates answered this question correctly. Distractor B was the most common incorrect answer. Candidates are reminded that solid metals react by losing electrons to become cations.
notes.10: This question required careful reading to identify the correct answer. Relative masses are always given on the atomic scale and so all options which do not reference an atom (or one atom) must be incorrect. The relative atomic mass is calculated from an average of the isotopes to give a single value.
notes.16: During a chemical reaction, if a substance is oxidised or reduced it must be one of the reactants on the left- hand side of the reaction arrow. A quarter of the candidates chose Distractor B or Distractor C, which are both reaction products.
notes.19: Across all the candidates the four options were equally chosen. Weaker candidates favoured Distractor A but the only non-metal oxide present was carbon dioxide.
notes.21: Four out of five of the weaker candidates chose Distractor B or Distractor C which both describe an increase in metallic character. Candidates are advised to use the Periodic Table provided to check their answer by referring to the position of elements they know well such as iron or oxygen.
notes.25: This question was not well answered. Many candidates did not recall or check that helium only has two outer shell electrons. Statement 1 is therefore incorrect. Most candidates chose Distractor B.
notes.27: This question was not well answered. Almost half of the candidates chose Distractor A. Although statement 2 is a correct statement it does not answer the question to explain why aluminium is used in place of copper for power cables. It would explain the reverse argument.
notes.35: All four options were equally chosen by candidates. Candidates should recall that alcohol compounds contain the –OH group and carboxylic acid contain the –COOH group which will help in eliminating the options in this question.
notes.36: Candidates are advised to use a mnemonic generator to devise a method to recall the order of the petroleum fractions. Most candidates suggested Distractor B, reversing the order of gasoline and naphtha fractions.
notes.40: Although most candidates correctly identified the colour produced by sodium ions in a flame test, many candidates did not recognise that effervescence after the addition of a dilute acid indicated either a pure metal or a carbonate compound. Distractor A was the most common answer.
notes.general_comments: Candidates found this to be an accessible paper overall with many questions showing good discrimination between candidates. Few candidates scored the very highest marks though. Overall candidates found Question 1, 4, 14, 33, and 39 to have the least challenge.
